extracted.intended_audience: readers, book buyers, librarians, collectors and booksellers browsing a publisher's catalogue (Chatto & Windus)
extracted.subtask_description: A commercial catalogue page listing books published by Chatto & Windus with descriptive blurbs, edition/format/specification details, reviewer quotes, and production notes for each title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of original illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editions should include the original illustrations where applicable (e.g., 'with all the Original Illustrations', 'with Spirited Coloured Illustrations by Cruikshank').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many entries emphasize 'with all the Original Illustrations', 'nearly 350 very fine Coloured pictures', '22 Illustrations after the inimitable designs of George Cruikshank' as a selling point; anti-patterns are editions that omit or mutilate original plates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful facsimile / accurate reprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile reprints should be true to the original editions and plates (e.g., 'reduced in exact facsimile of the Original Plates', 'An exact reprint', 'unmutilated Reprint of the First Edition').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance stresses faithful reproduction of plates/engravings and texts, inclusion of frontispieces and engraved title-pages, and truthful reduction in size when necessary ('reduced in size, but yet truthfully reproduced').

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition revision and editorial apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: New or reissued editions should be edited, revised, and supplied with introductory material or notes (e.g., 'A New Edition, edited by...', 'Edited, with an Introduction, by...', 'Revised and Corrected, with numerous Illustrations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalogue often specifies 'Edited, with an Introduction', 'With Notes', 'revised and corrected', 'With Life, Portrait, and numerous Illustrations' as part of edition quality; inclusion of critical/biographical apparatus is presented as value-add.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of work or series
rubrics_metrics.description: Works and series should be 'complete' or 'complete in one volume' when so advertised (e.g., 'Both Series complete in One Volume', 'Each Series is Complete in itself', 'complete, including...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness is repeatedly used as a selling point — 'complete in one volume', 'complete works', or 'Series complete' — implying editorial comprehensiveness and value for collectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical binding and finishing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical production quality: bindings and finishes such as 'cloth extra', 'gilt', 'gilt edges', 'half-morocco', 'handsomely bound'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many items list 'cloth extra, gilt, gilt edges', or special framed editions (e.g., 'handsomely framed and glazed, in carved oak'); these features are signalled as markers of higher-quality/collector editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper and printing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of high-quality or specialised paper and careful printing (e.g., 'printed on fine plate paper', 'printed on antique laid paper', 'carefully printed on fine paper').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalogue emphasizes 'beautifully printed', 'carefully printed on fine paper', and specific papers for facsimiles and large-paper copies as indicators of premium production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of paratextual materials (portraits, maps, plans, appendices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editions often include frontispieces, portraits, maps, plans, appendices, indexes, and other supplementary material (e.g., 'With Portrait and Plans', 'With a Map and 80 Illustrations', 'With an Appendix containing information...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These extras are listed as part of the edition's scholarly or practical utility: 'A full Translation, with Notes', 'An Appendix... containing the Fares', 'an elaborate Index refers to every name'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of edition presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Series or authors' works offered in a 'Uniform Edition' with consistent format across volumes (e.g., 'Uniform Edition, each Complete in One Volume').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform binding/format (same size, cloth, gilt design) is presented as desirable for collectors who want matching sets; price/format consistency often accompanies this claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and size specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear specification of physical format/size (e.g., 'Crown 8vo', 'Royal 16mo', '4to', 'large fcap. 8vo') as part of the listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The catalogue consistently lists format (which affects page size/layout and price) — useful for buyers and librarians seeking particular formats (illustrated 4to vs. crown 8vo, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special and large-paper copies / presentation copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of special issues such as 'Large-paper Copies', framed/hand-coloured editions, or limited/handsomely produced variants (e.g., 'a few Large Paper copies have been printed', 'handsomely framed and glazed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variants are highlighted with distinct pricing and described as limited or decorative options for collectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price transparency and tiering
rubrics_metrics.description: Every entry gives price and occasionally alternative prices for different bindings/editions (e.g., 'cloth extra, 7s. 6d.; or gilt edges, 6s.', 'in 2 vols., 8vo, cloth extra, 15s.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prices and format/binding options are given explicitly, signalling the commercial positioning and helping purchasers choose by budget and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly / historical usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Some works are marketed for their research/value to scholars (e.g., 'Must be consulted by all future biographers', 'chiefly collected on the spot by the Author', 'with Genealogical and Historical Annotations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of new or curious material, careful indexing, and original-source work are used to signal value for historians, genealogists, and biographers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility and clarity for technical manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical/practical books are judged by clarity, simplicity, and utility for practitioners (e.g., 'gives directions, in the simplest form, for assay of the baser metals', 'the instructions are clear and precise', 'indispensable to the young man seeking fortune in mining countries').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalogue entries for practical guides emphasize 'clear and precise' instructions, tables, and illustrative woodcuts as markers of usefulness to miners/explorers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary and artistic merit (reviewed claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Blurb and review excerpts cite literary/artistic qualities such as 'technical perfection of structure and melody', 'masterfulness of touch' in illustrations, 'vigorous and picturesque', 'one of the noblest poetical works', and 'eminently interesting'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reviewer-quoted attributes are used as evaluative criteria for literary and artistic success: technical mastery, intrinsic beauty, vigor/picturesqueness, imaginative power, and interest to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and faithfulness of reproductions of plates/engravings
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile or collected works should include engraved plates, wood-engravings, copper plates, frontispieces, and title-page facsimiles where original issues contained them (e.g., 'with Frontispiece and Engraved Title-page', 'with all the Wood Engravings, Plates, Memoirs, and Notes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalogue stresses that facsimile reprints include the full complement of original illustrations and plates, not just the text, as part of fidelity to the source.
